newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Suspended Romanian investment fund restarts.
newsitem.headline: Suspended Romanian investment fund restarts.

text.p: Troubled Romanian investment fund Credit Fond resumed trading on Monday after a 90-day suspension with investors voting to continue it as an open ended fund managed by current administrator Certinvest SA.
But investors redeeming their units will get only half of the pre-suspension value and some will have to wait for part of their money until a depository bank turns liquid.

"Some 45 percent of our investors agreed on continuation of Credit Fond as an open-ended fund managed by Certinvest, around 39 percent were for its transformation into a close-ended fund, with Certinvest as manager, and the rest were for other variants," Certinvest president Eugen Voicu told Reuters.
Credit Fond, which used to be among the largest of Romania's 12 investment funds, has some 17,000 investors.
Capital market regulator CNVM suspended it for 60 days in May after Certinvest cancelled the management contract following loss of confidence in the fund industry.
The move followed the suspension of Romania's largest fund FMOA after its units fell 45 percent, or $71 million, following the introduction of a new CNVM net asset valuation method.
Credit Fond's suspension was extended by another 30 days in July after investors requested more time to consider its fate.
Voicu said Credit Fond would concentrate on redeeming units on its restart.
He said people who had applied for redemption prior to suspension would get 60 percent of the value from several banks and 40 percent from troubled Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA.
"As Credit Bank does not have liquidity at present, people will get interest on the 40 percent stake for the period until the bank can start payments," Voicu said.
Credit Bank was taken to court by the National Bank which asked for its reorganisation after liquidity shortages prevented it making payments for more than a month.
Investors claiming redemption of their units after Monday will immediately get back the equivalent of 5.0 percent of the total number of their units, Voicu said.
The new value of a unit is 11,854 lei -- slightly more than half the 23,450 lei it was worth before fund suspension -- and this is the value at which redemptions are made, Voicu said.
